newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Environmental group urges Siemens boycott.
newsitem.headline: Environmental group urges Siemens boycott.

text.p: A Belgian environmental organisation said on Tuesday it and others were calling for a boycott of products by Siemens AG to persuade the German company to stop work on a controversial nuclear plant in Slovakia.

Voor Moeder Aarde (For Mother Earth) said German and Austrian politicians and environmental organisations from 60 countries had sent an open letter to Siemens and the Slovak government demanding a halt to work on the Mochovce plant.
The group said it had joined a network of over 400 other environmental organisations and elected politicians putting pressure on the Slovak government.

Voor Moeder Aarde said: "Mochovce is a first major step for Siemens in this region, where a number of (Soviet-era VVER 440/213) reactors are unfinished. In most cases these cannot be finalised without the support of western money."
Together with Siemens, the Slovak government is renovating Mochovce to turn it into a western-style nuclear plant.

Voor Moeder Aarde said unfinished plants of the Mochovce design in eastern Germany had been left untouched after German unification since the costs of bringing the plants up to western safety standards would be too high.
The first block of the plant, located 180 km (120 miles) east of Bratislava, is due to completed by the end of June 1998 and the second by the end of March 1999.
The plant has been widely criticised by western environmentalists as outdated, dangerous and unreliable.
